analysis.answer: Current law allows a person 21 or older to possess up to one ounce of cannabis without penalty. The proposed measure makes possessing any amount of cannabis a misdemeanor punishable by up to 90 days in jail.

Direct costs include enforcement resources for police, prosecutors, public defenders, courts, and jails. Opportunity costs include the loss of employment, housing, or other opportunities for individuals who acquire a criminal record due to a conviction.

Some individuals may reduce or hide their cannabis use to avoid criminal penalties, while an illicit market may expand to serve remaining demand. The criminal justice system will likely process more misdemeanor cases, diverting resources from other areas.
The measure addresses the use and availability of cannabis by establishing criminal penalties to deter possession. In doing so, it creates criminal records for users and increases enforcement costs.
